newsitem.title: USA: Probe continues into Indiana hospital deaths.
newsitem.headline: Probe continues into Indiana hospital deaths.

text.p: A lengthy investigation into whether dozens of deaths at an Indiana hospital were homicides or mercy killings remained inconclusive, police said Monday.

Experts continued to examine records and the remains of some patients who died at the hospital between 1993 and 1995, said Sgt. Mark Hartman, the Indiana State Police investigator in charge of the case. The investigation has been underway since March 1995 and a number of bodies were exhumed.

Hartman said police originally believed that 75 to 100 of more than 150 deaths at Vermillion County Hospital in Clinton could have been questionable. But he said no conclusions were drawn and the county prosecutor had not formed a grand jury for possible action.

Published reports have named as a suspect a licensed practical nurse who worked at the hospital's intensive care unit and who was present when most of the deaths occurred. He has not been charged but his nursing license was suspended.
